comments.author: @ChrizzeeB
comments.text:
Wes you need to approach the question considering inference more than training.
Jensen Huang explained this really well yesterday.

The unit cost of training is still dropping, and the scale of its processing. But there are certainly greater diminishing marginal returns.

However, the volume of inference done addressing a given prompt is where the benefits are greater.

If Training is X good;
You one-shot prompt - it predict the next word or whatever.
Better training gives a somewhat better answer. Up to a point, where the answer is statistically correct..

The inference: imagine you have a 100 million tokens to break down the prompt, ask it in a hundred ways, reevaluate, critique, and eventually find the ultimate answer. 
-> this is where the returns are still palpably scaling.

Everyone seems to be confusing a larger foundational model, with a greater inference stack. Until these topics are approached separately, no valid discussion will be had.

It’s hard to believe AI development could just be "stalling" right now. If we’re seeing signs of slowing down, it might not be due to any real technical limitations.
